key_insight: Trajectory replay updates continuous-time generative models while preserving prior tasks by matching historical and incoming velocity fields instead of repeatedly generating replay samples.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support continual updates of generative engineering surrogates, but the abstract reports no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Match a frozen historical velocity field along its trajectories and the incoming task's velocity field.
Balance retention and adaptation with a stability–plasticity coefficient, yielding density-weighted velocity mixing.
Use mean velocity distillation to access historical trajectories with few network evaluations per update.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better class-incremental image generation than generative replay and distillation baselines, plus two biological case studies preserving treatment-effect prediction across new contexts and batches.
watch_item: Engineering deployment would require validating physical consistency and sensitivity to the stability–plasticity coefficient.
paper_title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models
